vocabulary.meaning_en: travelling from place to place by train
vocabulary.example: Train travel is popular in Europe.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the area next to the tracks where you wait to get on a train
vocabulary.example: The train to London leaves from platform 3.

vocabulary.meaning_en: one of the parts of a train where passengers sit
vocabulary.note_ar: بريطاني؛ الأمريكي يقول car أو passenger car
vocabulary.example: Our seats are in the second carriage.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the place where you buy tickets
vocabulary.example: You can buy a return ticket at the ticket office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list of times when trains or buses arrive and leave
vocabulary.note_ar: الأمريكي يقول schedule ويُنطق /ˈskedʒuːl/، والبريطاني قد ينطقه /ˈʃedjuːl/
vocabulary.example: Check the timetable for the next train.
vocabulary.note_en: Americans say 'schedule', pronounced /ˈskedʒuːl/; British people may say /ˈʃedjuːl/.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person on a train who checks tickets
vocabulary.example: The conductor asked to see our tickets.

vocabulary.meaning_en: one of the metal bars that a train runs on
vocabulary.note_ar: railway بريطاني، railroad أمريكي = السكة الحديد
vocabulary.example: Don't walk on the rails.
vocabulary.note_en: 'Railway' is British, 'railroad' is American: the train track system.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a fast train that stops at only a few stations
vocabulary.example: Take the express train; it's much faster.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a train with beds for long night journeys
vocabulary.example: We took the sleeper train to the south.

vocabulary.meaning_en: travelling from place to place by bus
vocabulary.example: Bus travel is cheaper than flying.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place on the road where buses stop for passengers
vocabulary.example: I waited at the bus stop for 20 minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large place where many buses start and end their routes
vocabulary.example: The bus station is near the city centre.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who drives a vehicle
vocabulary.example: The driver stopped to let us get off.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way a bus or train goes from start to end
vocabulary.example: This bus route goes past the museum.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a bus with two floors
vocabulary.example: London is famous for its red double-decker buses.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a comfortable bus for long journeys or tours
vocabulary.example: We travelled to the coast by coach.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the money you pay to travel on public transport
vocabulary.example: The bus fare went up this year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper or card that shows you have paid
vocabulary.example: Did you buy the tickets?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where you sit
vocabulary.example: Is this seat free?

vocabulary.meaning_en: an arrangement to keep a seat or room for you
vocabulary.example: I made a reservation for two seats.
vocabulary.note_en: 'Reserved seats' = seats that are booked for someone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: travelling from one place to another, often long
vocabulary.example: The journey took ten hours.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the trip you make every day between home and work or school
vocabulary.example: My commute to work is 40 minutes.
vocabulary.note_en: A 'commuter' is someone who travels to work or school every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: arriving after the expected time
vocabulary.example: Hurry! We're late again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: as said or shown by
vocabulary.example: According to the timetable, the train leaves at nine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in fact, really
vocabulary.example: Did you actually buy the tickets?
vocabulary.note_en: It does not mean 'at the moment'; for that use 'currently'.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long seat for several people, often made of wood
vocabulary.example: We sat on a wooden bench in the park.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to force someone to leave a place
vocabulary.note_ar: وتعني أيضاً: يرمي شيئاً في القمامة
vocabulary.example: The conductor threw them out of the train.
vocabulary.note_en: It also means to put something in the rubbish.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move or do something very quickly
vocabulary.example: They rushed onto the train.
vocabulary.note_en: 'Rush hour' = the busiest time of day for traffic.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to suddenly lose consciousness for a short time
vocabulary.example: She almost fainted from the heat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the general activity of going from place to place
vocabulary.example: I love travel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a whole visit to a place: going, staying and coming back
vocabulary.example: How was your business trip?

vocabulary.meaning_en: money you pay for a service, entry or official process
vocabulary.example: You must pay the visa fee at the embassy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the system of tracks that trains use
vocabulary.example: The railway connects the two cities.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a passenger who gives the driver unwanted advice; anyone who tries to control what is not their job
vocabulary.meaning_ar: شخص يتدخل ويعطي توجيهات غير مطلوبة
vocabulary.example: Stop being a back-seat driver and let me drive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a very loud noise made by something moving extremely fast
vocabulary.example: The train made a sonic boom as it left the tunnel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small bright bird that dives to catch fish
vocabulary.example: A kingfisher dived into the river without a splash.

fine_lines.title: travel vs journey vs trip
fine_lines.explanation_ar: travel هو النشاط العام للسفر، أي الانتقال من مكان لآخر بشكل عام. journey تركز على الطريق نفسه: المسافة والوقت والجهد المبذول من نقطة إلى نقطة، وغالباً تكون طويلة أو متعبة. trip هي الرحلة الكاملة: الذهاب والإقامة والعودة، وغالباً لها هدف محدد كالعمل أو الإجازة.

examples.sentence: The journey took ten hours by train.

fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Travel' is the general activity of going from place to place. 'Journey' focuses on the way itself: the distance, time and effort from one point to another, and it is often long or tiring. 'Trip' is the whole visit: going, staying and coming back, usually with a clear purpose like work or a holiday.

fine_lines.title: fare vs fee vs ticket
fine_lines.explanation_ar: fare هي الأجرة التي تدفعها للمواصلات العامة فقط (قطار، حافلة، تاكسي). fee رسوم تدفعها مقابل خدمة احترافية أو دخول مكان أو معاملة رسمية مثل رسوم التأشيرة أو المدرسة. ticket هي الورقة أو البطاقة التي تثبت أنك دفعت.

examples.sentence: The train fare to Paris is expensive.
You have to pay the visa fee at the embassy.
Show your ticket to the conductor.

fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Fare' is the money you pay for public transport only (train, bus, taxi). A 'fee' is money you pay for a professional service, to enter a place, or for official paperwork, like a visa fee or school fees. A 'ticket' is the paper or card that shows you have paid.

fine_lines.title: timetable vs schedule
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما جدول مواعيد القطارات والحافلات. timetable أشيع في بريطانيا، و schedule أشيع في أمريكا، وكلاهما مفهوم في كل مكان.

examples.sentence: The new bus timetable starts on Monday.
The train is running on schedule.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean a list of times for trains and buses. 'Timetable' is more common in Britain and 'schedule' in America, but both are understood everywhere.

fine_lines.title: bus stop vs bus station
fine_lines.explanation_ar: bus stop مكان صغير على الطريق تقف فيه الحافلة لركوب ونزول الركاب. bus station مبنى أو مكان كبير تبدأ منه الحافلات وتنتهي إليه خطوطها.

examples.sentence: Get off at the next bus stop.
All coaches leave from the main bus station.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A 'bus stop' is a small place by the road where the bus stops to let people on and off. A 'bus station' is a big building or area where bus routes start and end.

expressions.meaning_ar: شخص يتدخل ويعطي نصائح وتوجيهات غير مطلوبة
expressions.example: I don't need a back-seat driver; I know how to run this project.
expressions.meaning_en: someone who gives advice and instructions nobody asked for

expressions.example: Our train is on platform five.
According to the timetable, the bus comes every 15 minutes.
expressions.meaning_en: as shown in the list of times

expressions.example: No tickets and no money? We're doomed!
expressions.meaning_en: we are in big trouble (said to exaggerate)

expressions.example: If you don't have a ticket, they'll throw you out.
expressions.meaning_en: to make someone leave a place

expressions.example: He's on a business trip in Dubai this week.

grammar.title: Future perfect simple: will have + past participle
grammar.explanation_ar: تخيّل أنك سافرت بآلة الزمن إلى نقطة في المستقبل ونظرت إلى الوراء: هناك أفعال ستكون قد انتهت قبل تلك النقطة. التركيب: الفاعل + will have + التصريف الثالث. وغالباً نستخدم معه by (بحلول). النفي: will not have، والسؤال يبدأ بـ Will.
examples: By tomorrow morning, they will have arrived.
By next week, I will not have finished the book.
Will you have eaten by 8 p.m.?
By the end of the month, I will have booked the ticket.
grammar.explanation_en: Imagine you travel in a time machine to a point in the future and look back: some actions will already be finished before that point. Form: subject + will have + past participle (3rd form of the verb). We often use 'by' (meaning 'not later than') with it. Negative: will not have. Questions start with 'Will'.

questions.question: The ___ took ten hours by train. (focus on the long way itself)
questions.explanation_ar: journey تركز على الطريق والمسافة والجهد.
questions.explanation_en: 'Journey' focuses on the way, the distance and the effort.

questions.question: How was your business ___?
questions.explanation_ar: trip هي الرحلة الكاملة بهدف محدد كالعمل.
questions.explanation_en: A 'trip' is a whole visit with a clear purpose, like work.

questions.question: You must pay the visa ___ at the embassy.
questions.explanation_ar: fee رسوم مقابل خدمة أو معاملة رسمية.
questions.explanation_en: A 'fee' is money paid for a service or official paperwork.

questions.question: The bus ___ is two dollars.
questions.explanation_en: 'Fare' is the price of public transport.

questions.question: By tomorrow morning, they ___.
questions.explanation_ar: حدث سينتهي قبل نقطة في المستقبل = will have + التصريف الثالث.
questions.explanation_en: An action that will be finished before a point in the future = will have + past participle.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
choices: By next week, I will have not finish the book.
By next week, I will not have finished the book.
By next week, I not will have finished the book.
By next week, I won't finished the book.
questions.explanation_ar: النفي: will not have + التصريف الثالث.
questions.explanation_en: Negative: will not have + past participle.

questions.question: A "back-seat driver" is someone who:
choices: gives unwanted advice about things that aren't their job
questions.explanation_ar: back-seat driver شخص يتدخل ويوجه دون أن يُطلب منه.
questions.explanation_en: A back-seat driver interferes and gives directions without being asked.

questions.question: In American English, a train "carriage" is usually called a:
questions.explanation_ar: carriage بريطاني، و car أو passenger car أمريكي.
questions.explanation_en: 'Carriage' is British; Americans say 'car' or 'passenger car'.

questions.question: Your daily trip from home to work is your:
questions.explanation_ar: commute = التنقل اليومي بين البيت والعمل.
questions.explanation_en: 'Commute' = your daily travel between home and work.
